newsitem.title: QATAR: U.S. marines stage naval exercises in Qatar.
newsitem.headline: U.S. marines stage naval exercises in Qatar.

text.p: Around 700 U.S. marines and sailors have begun a military training exercise in the Gulf state of Qatar, U.S. Marine Corps officials said on Saturday.

The exercise, codenamed "Native Fury '97", involves loading off a ship nearly 1,500 pieces of equipment, including tanks, amphibious assault vehicles, light armoured vehicles, artillery, trucks, ammunition and supplies which could sustain a 16,500-strong taskforce for 30 days of combat.

"It is designed to improve readiness and training for the marines and sailors while building upon the relations with our brothers in arms in the region," said Brigadier General Edward Langston of the U.S. Marine Corps.
"With this technique, a large Marine force can project power ashore in a very short time," he told reporters at Messai'eed port, about 50 km (30 miles) south of the capital Doha.
Langston said the exercise was not motivated by any conflict in the region. "But as there is always tension in this region we are here to stabilise...We are always part of a U.S. strategy."
The equipment was downloaded from the maritime preposition ship MV Pvt Franklin Phillips, which sailed to Qatar from a U.S. base on the island of Diego Garcia in the Indian Ocean.
"The Qatari navy is not taking part in the exercises this time, but we hope to do some work with the local coast guard," Langston said.
This is the U.S. Marines' second such training exercise in Qatar. The Qatari navy took part in the first exercise, codenamed "Indigo Desert", which was held in October 1995.
The Phillips is one of 13 prepositioning ships used by the U.S. Marines to ferry heavy military material and supplies to and from battle zones.

Doha is the site of two U.S. military warehouses. But Langston said the tanks, artillery and other military equipment used in the current exercise would not be left behind. "All equipment will be taken back," he told Reuters.
A Marine Corps public affairs officer said the force planned to set sail for another country from Qatar on October 26 to stage similar exercises. He would not name the country.
